candidate.title: MeDIP-Seq / DIP-seq
candidate.scope: The shared methylated-DNA enrichment row headed MeDIP-Seq / DIP-seq in the supplied Illumina poster crop, from methylated genomic DNA represented on nucleosomes to purified enriched DNA. Neighboring TAB-Seq, MIRA and hMeDIP-Seq rows, and the disconnected Pyridine icon at the right, are outside this assigned row. The row depicts one serial route, not separate pooled branches. Library construction and sequencing are named/described interfaces beyond the drawn DNA endpoint; their internal operations are not drawn. The biological target in this row is 5-methylcytosine-associated genomic regions; sequence representation is obtained through preferential recovery of genomic DNA fragments. The primary references resolve this as a MeDIP-Seq depiction and a 5mC implementation within DIP-seq, rather than establishing that the two names have identical complete protocols.

operations.label: Immunoprecipitate
operations.description: Capture the red-marked DNA fragments with pink antibodies, enriching the retained antibody-associated fraction relative to the pale unbound fragments.
operations.mechanism: Anti-5mC antibodies recognize methylated DNA and retain an antibody-associated, methylation-enriched fraction. Binding is the depicted selection mechanism; antibody specificity and selectivity require validation rather than implying perfect recovery or purity.
operations.information_effect: Genomic DNA is both the modification-bearing substrate and the source of the sequenced library inserts. Preferential recovery associates the represented sequence region with 5mC recognition. Capture alone does not identify every modified cytosine or provide an absolute methylation fraction; enrichment depends on modification density and antibody performance.

method_scopes.rationale: All four drawn operations apply to the methylated-DNA enrichment implementation of MeDIP-Seq. The candidate collection page is verified by its MeDIP-Seq/DIP-seq heading and caption A schematic overview of MeDIP-seq; it specifies anti-5mC capture. The literal Down et al. reference matches PMID 18612301 (Nat Biotechnol 26:779–785, 2008), whose full text explicitly describes MeDIP-seq. The paper ligates Illumina adapters to fragmented DNA before MeDIP and amplifies the enriched product afterward. These paper-supported interface details clarify that the schematic is abbreviated; the drawing does not specify adapter state and is preserved without inserting unshown library-construction operations. The paper distinguishes its MeDIP-chip LM-PCR procedure from MeDIP-seq, so that named subprotocol is not added.

checks.rationale: Complete independent inspection supports the declared schematic scope and architecture. Both grouped targets are retained, with DIP-seq explicitly restricted to the drawn 5mC implementation. Six material states and four local operations represent every transformation in this row; nine flows preserve the serial route and antibody association. The two-input capture is one joint binding operation, not collapsed independent processing. There is no depicted retained alternative or pooled branch. Genomic fragments carry the sequence readout and enrichment history; antibodies are binding reagents. Unshown adapters, terminal chemistry and library internals are left unspecified. The plain final DNA icon is reasonably interpreted as schematic simplification, with no claim of demethylation. Literal references, all nine paper associations, both method assignments and readout limitations have been checked. No consequential correction or blocking unknown is required.
